findings.where: First screen at both widths (hero and nav: Profile, Articles, Blog), and the whole page. The palette names a pad-yellow 'address strip', and the texture note says it sits 'at the foot of the sheet', but no such strip is on the page
findings.fault: There is no way to reach Mark anywhere on the page. The first screen has no action at all: no email address, no mailto link and no Contact item in the nav. parts.txt lists only the logo, three nav links, a download link and the replay button. The yellow address panel the specimen describes was never built, so the brief's one personal route to Mark is missing. So is the shown address (Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com).
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who has just read the line and wants to write to Mark can find no address. The founder also objects: the personal-advisor test needs 'one direct, personal way to reach him', and the brief requires one action with the address shown on the first screen.

findings.where: Motion section: the whole panel, at both widths
findings.fault: The motion sketch sits on a large saturated lilac/lavender block. That colour is in none of the tile's four palette roles, it isn't the house blue or grey, and nothing explains it. It is the loudest area on the page and breaks the calm ivory paper with grey and blue ink that the direction promises. It also contradicts the palette note that the purple stage backdrop gets turned to ink.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for blue and grey as the only ink and one soft ground. Mark, for whom a stray lilac reads as playful rather than legal-journal serious.

findings.where: Article specimen: the subheads 'So, what are the key ‘chapter topics’?' and 'Download', at both widths
findings.fault: Both subheads are set in a heavy, wide black grotesque. It belongs to neither face of the type pair, although the specimen promises Newsreader 500 for subheads. The pair is a light serif and plain Public Sans, and this face shouts against both and breaks the paper's refined voice.
findings.who_objects: Mark and the founder, who asked for serious type and nothing loud or techy. Angélique, whose subheads would carry this off-system face on every article.

findings.where: Article specimen: the title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law'
findings.fault: The title is a heavy bold serif, a weight the type pair never names (Light 300 display, 400 reading, 500 subheads). It sits apart from the hero's light, high-contrast line, so the article page and the homepage don't look like one hand.
findings.who_objects: A reader moving from the homepage to an article sees a different voice. The founder, judging whether the type system holds across both surfaces.

findings.fault: Each swatch is a different shape: an outlined square-cornered box, a rounded filled box, an ellipse, and a square box with a blue border. Four samples of one kind get four treatments. The yellow swatch's blue edge looks like a selected or focused state, and the ellipse looks like a button or a token rather than a colour chip.
findings.who_objects: The founder, reading the palette to judge the colours, has to wonder whether the shapes and the blue edge mean something.

findings.where: Article specimen: the Download block at desktop
findings.fault: At desktop the link title sits at the left and its 'Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF' line is pushed to the far right of the column. The file's type and date are separated from the link they describe.
findings.who_objects: A reader deciding whether to download a PDF looks for its type and date beside the title and may miss them.

findings.where: First screen at phone width: the portrait
findings.fault: At phone width the portrait is inset inside the hairline frame with margins on all sides. At desktop it is flush against the frame, and the texture note says the portrait is 'set flush against it'. The one borrowed detail, the document edge, is treated differently at the two widths.
findings.who_objects: The founder, judging whether the frame works as the document's edge, sees it working only at desktop.
